newsitem.title: NAMIBIA: SAB UNLIKELY TO GET NAMIBIA PLANT GO-AHEAD.
newsitem.headline: SAB UNLIKELY TO GET NAMIBIA PLANT GO-AHEAD.

text.p: The Namibian government's opposition to South African Breweries (SAB) opening a bottling plant was unlikely to change, Namibian Trade and Industry Minister Hidipo Hamutenya said on Tuesday.
"We will not allow a foreign monopoly to come in and destroy a successful local enterprise and we have not changed our opinion on that", Hamutenya told Reuters.
"South African Breweries almost totally own the Southern African market," he said. "Why should they want to take over Namibia as well?"
SAB applied to set up a N$100 million bottling plant in Oshakati some 700 km north of the Namibian capital Windhoek in June this year.
But the Namibian government has objected to the plant, fearing it will pose a threat to the local market which is dominated by Namibian Breweries Ltd (NBL) .
With a planned capacity of 250,000 hectolitres of beer a year, the brewery could swallow up to 40 percent of NBL's estimated market.
It is estimated that South African Breweries controls 98 percent of the regional market, with Namibia Breweries Limited its only competitor.
As part of its proposal, SAB has offered a 51 percent stake in the bottling facility to a consortium of Namibian businessmen.
Hamutenya said the offer was "nothing but another attempt to try and capture the Namibian market".
Hamutenya also rejected SAB's claim that it would not only supply the local market through the bottling plant at Oshakati.
"If they want to supply other markets they can easily do so from their other plants all over southern Africa," he said.
Local papers reported members of the local consortium to partner SAB in the project as saying they would take up the issue with the government if the proposal was turned down.
They said the government would be denying previously disadvantaged groups a stake in the economy.
But Hamutenya disagreed, saying: "All SAB is trying to do is to get in the back-door by lobbying local support. This is nothing new and as far as I'm concerned it will not help change our stance."
